prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry to hear you were injured — that’s stressful. I can help you pick the right lawyer, but first a couple quick questions so I can tailor my advice:
- How serious are your injuries (minor, ER/hospital, long‑term/disability)?
- Was the other driver clearly at fault, or is fault disputed?
- Has a police report been taken and have you contacted any insurers yet?
- Do you prefer a local Pleasanton lawyer, or are you okay with a lawyer from elsewhere in the Bay Area?

While you answer, here are practical steps and guidance you can use immediately and when choosing a lawyer.

Immediate steps (do these now if you haven’t):
- Get medical care and follow up — your health and medical records are critical evidence.
- Preserve evidence: photos of the vehicles, scene, your injuries, contact info for witnesses, dashcam/phone footage.
- Get a copy of the police report and accident report number.
- Don’t give a recorded statement to the other party’s insurer without lawyer advice. You may tell your own insurer facts but avoid speculation.
- Note deadlines: in California the general personal‑injury statute of limitations is 2 years from the date of injury (longer/shorter in special cases or if a government agency is involved).

What kind of lawyer you should hire
- For car accident injuries, hire a personal injury attorney who focuses on car collisions and has experience with California auto insurance law.
- If injuries are severe (catastrophic, brain/spinal injury, permanent disability) look for lawyers with experience handling high‑value, complex cases and access to medical and vocational experts.

How to find good candidates (Pleasanton / Tri‑Valley / Alameda County)
- Alameda County Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service (they vet lawyers).
- California State Bar website to confirm licensing and look up disciplinary history.
- Look for local attorneys with consistent positive client reviews, trial experience (if the case might go to court), and active handling of car accident cases.
- Ask friends, family, or medical providers for recommendations.

What to ask at a free initial consultation
- How long have you handled car-accident injury cases? How many cases like mine have you handled?
- What percentage of your practice is personal injury / auto collisions?
- Do you handle cases on a contingency fee? What is your contingency fee and what costs would be deducted?
- Who will handle my case day‑to‑day (the named attorney or staff/associates)?
- Do you go to trial when necessary? What is your trial record?
- Ask for examples of outcomes in similar cases (settlement ranges or verdicts).
- How will you communicate (phone/email/text) and how often?

Typical fee and cost expectations (California)
- Most PI attorneys work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Typical percentages: ~33% if settled before a lawsuit, up to 40% or more if suit and trial are necessary (some firms use sliding scales).
- You may also be responsible for case costs (filing fees, expert fees) that are typically reimbursed from your recovery.

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount.
- Pressure to sign immediately without reviewing terms.
- Attorneys who won’t put fee agreement in writing or who have unclear billing for costs.

What to bring to consultations
- Photos of the accident and injuries, police report, medical records, bills, pay stubs for lost wages, communications from insurers, and vehicle repair estimates.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a short message you can send to lawyers to ask for a consultation.
- Provide a checklist to compare attorneys after consultations.
- Narrow the search: give me your ZIP code or whether you prefer Pleasanton vs. nearby cities, and I can list well‑known local firms and how to contact them.

Which specific lawyer should you hire?
- I can’t endorse one single person without knowing more about your case and preferences. If you tell me your ZIP code and the injury severity, I’ll find a short list of reputable local personal injury lawyers and give recommendations on which to contact first.
